name: lcry_lamp_13
description: Parametric square LCRY lamp set by a WIFI/PSCN pulse on top, cleared by WIFI/NSCN on the bottom.
why: Console lamp bank pattern (build-lessons 'control console pattern'): PSCN must touch LCRY directly, so a 1px WIFI->PSCN nub feeds the top of the slab and a WIFI->NSCN nub taps the bottom; sparking the top channel lights the lamp, the bottom channel is the reset/return path. v2 hardening (blueprint_lint had 2 critical heat_source_uninsulated findings, one per WIFI): each WIFI cell is widened by 1 row (extending away from its PSCN/NSCN neighbor, not into it) so a full INSL ring can wrap all 4 sides while the original PSCN/NSCN contact -- the actual set/reset signal entry -- stays touching the WIFI cell exactly as captured. The pre-existing pscn_not_touching_lcry warnings on the 13x13 body are left as-is: they are the module's documented, intentional design (the 1px nub is the entire electrical interface; the body is only there to be visible from a distance), not a defect. Re-verified: blueprint_lint reports zero critical findings, compile ok.
source: save2, x187-199 y32-50 (one of four consoles lamps, x176-330 y28-62)
